proposals.title: Multimodal Integration for Robust Tissue Reorganization Mapping
proposals.summary: This analysis infers spatial domains and continuous cellular trajectories by integrating gene expression, spatial coordinates, and tissue morphology. It employs rigorous quality control and batch correction to mitigate inter-section variability and technical noise. Spatial neighborhood graphs are constructed to ensure that inferred cell–cell interactions are biologically plausible. The approach leverages image registration techniques to align morphological cues with transcriptomic data. Comprehensive validations against anatomical landmarks and sensitivity analyses underscore its relevance in studying development, injury, and disease.

proposals.title: Spatial Denoising and Imputation for Enhanced Transcriptomic Insights
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on the explicit modeling and mitigation of noise using advanced denoising and imputation techniques tailored for spatial transcriptomics data. It combines deep learning-based imputation models with classical statistical methods to recover dropout events and improve signal fidelity. Gene expression data are integrated with spatial coordinates and imaging features to refine local cellular contexts. Explicit spatial neighborhood constraints are imposed to ensure that imputed values respect tissue continuity. This method is designed to address the high noise levels typical of spatial assays and is highly relevant to studies of tissue reorganization under varying conditions.

proposals.title: Neighborhood-Constrained Trajectory Inference in Growing Tissues
proposals.summary: This analysis models continuous cellular trajectories within tissues undergoing growth and deformation. It incorporates gene expression profiles, spatial distances, and morphological images to capture dynamic cell state changes. Spatial neighborhoods are explicitly defined using distance thresholds and autocorrelation metrics to constrain trajectory inference. The approach accounts for tissue deformation by integrating cross-sectional image registration and sensitivity checks against known anatomical structures. This strategy is well-suited for exploring developmental, injury-induced, and disease-associated tissue remodeling.

proposals.title: Quantitative Spatial Graph Construction for Cell–Cell Communication
proposals.summary: This analysis constructs robust spatial graphs to infer and validate cell–cell communication events. Gene expression data are combined with spatial coordinates and high-resolution tissue images to build networks that reflect true cellular interactions. Distance-based thresholds and quantified autocorrelation metrics are used to filter out spurious ligand–receptor co-occurrences. The method also integrates batch correction to harmonize data across sections and platforms. By providing quantitative validation of the spatial graphs against known anatomical structures, this approach ensures that the inferred interactions are biologically plausible.

proposals.title: Batch-Corrected, Multi-Sectional Integration for Cross-Platform Analysis
proposals.summary: This proposal addresses the challenges of integrating spatial transcriptomics data collected from multiple sections and platforms. It applies rigorous batch-effect correction and section-specific normalization to harmonize gene expression profiles across different tissue slices. Advanced image registration techniques are used to align morphological data with spatial coordinates, ensuring consistent mapping of tissue architecture. Spatial neighborhood constraints are enforced to delineate coherent tissue domains and trajectories. This integrative framework is designed to robustly capture tissue reorganization events in diverse experimental settings.

proposals.title: Integrated Modeling of Spatial Domains and Denoised Trajectories
proposals.summary: This analysis identifies coherent spatial domains and infers cellular trajectories using a combination of expression profiles, spatial positioning, and morphological cues. It incorporates explicit noise denoising and imputation protocols to enhance data quality before downstream analyses. The method employs clustering algorithms on image-extracted features alongside transcriptomic data to define tissue compartments. Spatial graphs and trajectory inference techniques are then applied under strict neighborhood constraints. This strategy ensures robust reconstruction of tissue reorganization patterns and yields interpretable insights into cellular state transitions.

proposals.title: Deformation-Aware Spatial Transcriptomics for Tissue Remodeling
proposals.summary: This proposal introduces a deformation-aware framework to model tissue remodeling where growth and mechanical forces alter tissue geometry. It integrates gene expression, spatial coordinates, and morphological images to capture the effects of tissue deformation on cellular organization. Advanced image registration methods are used to correct for tissue distortions across sections. Spatial trajectories are inferred with explicit consideration of deformation parameters, ensuring accurate cell state mapping. This approach is validated using quantitative metrics and external anatomical references to underscore its utility in studying dynamic tissue changes.

proposals.title: Robust Ligand–Receptor Inference within Spatial Neighborhoods
proposals.summary: This analysis specifically targets the mapping of cell–cell communication by robustly inferring ligand–receptor interactions within spatially constrained neighborhoods. It integrates expression data with physical distances and tissue morphology to filter interactions based on spatial plausibility. Explicit distance thresholds and spatial autocorrelation metrics are employed to eliminate false positives. Batch correction and noise-reduction steps are applied to enhance the reliability of the inferred interactions. This method aims to accurately capture biologically relevant communication networks in complex tissue environments.

proposals.title: Deep Learning-Based Integration for Enhanced Spatial Imputation
proposals.summary: This proposal leverages deep learning approaches to integrate multi-modal spatial transcriptomics data and perform enhanced imputation of missing expression values. It fuses gene expression, spatial coordinates, and morphological image features into a unified model that corrects for dropout events and technical noise. A convolutional neural network is employed to extract meaningful features from tissue images, which are then combined with spatial graphs. The model enforces neighborhood constraints to maintain tissue context and generate smooth cellular trajectories. This deep integration is designed to boost data quality and interpretability in analyses of tissue reorganization.

proposals.title: Cross-Validated Spatial Integration with Rigorous Graph Metrics
proposals.summary: This analysis employs a rigorous and cross-validated framework to integrate spatial transcriptomics data across multiple modalities. It combines batch-corrected gene expression, precise spatial coordinates, and detailed morphological images to construct validated interaction networks. Quantitative graph metrics such as autocorrelation and sensitivity analysis are applied to ensure the reliability of spatial neighborhoods and cell–cell communication inferences. The approach also includes explicit measures for correcting section-specific variability and spatial distortions. By integrating statistical validation with multimodal data fusion, the method robustly maps tissue reorganization events relevant to development, injury, and disease.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analyses most likely performed in the hidden paper, via a three-step draft–critique–synthesis workflow that writes draft, critique, and final proposal JSON artifacts to the specified paths.

steps.title: Draft spatial-omics proposal set
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to generate an initial JSON draft of exactly 10 candidate computational spatial-omics analyses that are plausible for the hidden paper, grounded only in the provided background about integrating expression, spatial distance, and morphology across platforms. Save this draft as `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial planning agent is required to construct an initial, domain-aware set of candidate analyses that reflect the stated goals (tracing processes through neighboring locations, spatially plausible cell–cell communication, and noise/missing-data reduction under explicit neighborhood and modality constraints). This gives subsequent agents a concrete, machine-readable hypothesis set to refine.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step (1) must be handled by the Spatial-CV Planning Agent as required; spatial_cv_agent is purpose-built to draft exactly 10 spatial-omics analysis proposals and write the draft_proposals artifact.

steps.title: Critique draft proposals
steps.description: Use a Critic agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and produce a structured critique at `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` that evaluates each draft proposal for clarity, feasibility, redundancy, and alignment with the background aims (neighborhood-aware trajectories, spatially plausible communication, and denoising/imputation), and notes any missing conceptual coverage.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique step is needed to pressure-test the draft proposals before finalization, ensuring they collectively cover the key themes from the background, avoid unnecessary overlap, and stay within the constraints of computational spatial-omics analysis without executing any analysis.
steps.assignment_rationale: critic_agent is the dedicated review-only agent whose sole function is to read draft proposals and produce a structured critique.json artifact, matching the needs of step (2).

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use a hypothesis/final-synthesis agent to combine `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` into a refined final set of proposals saved as `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json`. The final file must be a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapping to an array of exactly 10 items, where each item contains only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing a distinct, computational spatial-omics analysis likely performed in the hidden paper, consistent with the provided background.
steps.reasoning: This synthesis step turns the critiqued draft into the required final deliverable, enforcing the exact JSON schema and cardinality (10 proposals) while integrating critique feedback so the final proposals are coherent, diverse, and maximally aligned with the problem setting described in the background.
steps.assignment_rationale: hypothesis_agent is explicitly designed for hypothesis proposal drafting and final synthesis and is the only agent that outputs final_proposals.json, making it the correct choice for step (3).

provenance.justification: The user prescribed a fixed three-step draft–critique–synthesis workflow with specific artifact paths and agent roles (spatial_cv_agent for drafting, Critic for critique, and a synthesis agent for the final proposals). This bespoke coordination pattern does not match the more elaborate, end-to-end analysis templates like paper_hypothesis_generation or hypothesis_testing, so the plan was written from scratch without reusing a template.
